pattern_name: FSE-Style Table-Driven FSM vs Nested If/Else
variant_desc: 8-state FSM decoded from 1M-byte input via nested if-else vs precomputed table (variant 2: seed=44, n_scale=1.5x)
source_citation: http://fastcompression.blogspot.com/2014/01/fse-decoding-how-it-works.html — Yann Collet (FSE inventor); confirmed by zstd PR #2722 (hand-written asm wraps C function precisely because table-driven C inner loop is ~40% slower than tuned asm)
novelty_rationale: Tests whether the LLM knows to lift a procedural per-byte state machine into a precomputed (state, input) -> (symbol, next_state) transition table built at init time. Compiler cannot synthesize the table from procedural state-update code. Unlike Huffman which incrementally shifts bits, FSE rewrites the entire state value, eliminating symbol-length-dependent control flow.
